subject.title: [Feature]: Listen — speak assistant messages aloud in the mobile apps

question: Should OpenClaw add a general `tts.speak` base64-audio Gateway RPC for mobile transcript playback, or should mobile reuse/extend existing `talk.speak` or `tts.convert` instead?
rationale: The request crosses a public Gateway method surface, first-party mobile UX, provider routing, and fallback semantics, and the issue already carries the protected maintainer label.

options.title: Add `tts.speak` and mobile Listen
options.body: Add a general remote-readable TTS RPC backed by `messages.tts`, then wire iOS and Android assistant bubbles to use it with native TTS fallback.

options.title: Reuse an existing method
options.body: Avoid a new protocol method by changing `tts.convert` or `talk.speak`, but first resolve the Talk-vs-general-TTS semantics and remote audio delivery contract.

options.title: Defer to Talk/mobile voice roadmap
options.body: Keep this open as a product-direction item until maintainers decide how transcript playback, Talk mode, and voice-note features should relate.

recommendation.title: Add `tts.speak` and mobile Listen
recommendation.body: Add a general remote-readable TTS RPC backed by `messages.tts`, then wire iOS and Android assistant bubbles to use it with native TTS fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete opened the issue and has the strongest recent history on the relevant gateway voice and shared mobile chat paths.
